discover_titles: Hawaii on Alert: Hurricane Lowell Brings Tropical Storm Warning
Category 3 Hurricane Lowell Nears Hawaii, Prompts Flood Warnings
Islands Brace for Impact: Hawaii Prepares for Hurricane Lowell
spot: Hawaii residents and visitors are urged to prepare for heavy rains, flooding, and potential mudslides as Hurricane Lowell, a major Category 3 storm, prompted a tropical storm warning for Kauai and Niihau on Sunday, September 6, 2026. The storm is forecast to pass west of the islands late Monday and Tuesday.
content_html:
Key Developments

Officials in Hawaii have issued a tropical storm warning for Kauai and Niihau as Hurricane Lowell, a powerful Category 3 storm, approaches the islands. The National Hurricane Center reported that Lowell, with maximum sustained winds of 125 mph (205 kph), was located approximately 575 miles (925 kilometers) south-southwest of Lihue on Sunday. It is moving north-northwest at 5 mph (7 kph) and is expected to pass west of the islands late Monday and Tuesday.

Forecasters anticipate significant rainfall, with Kauai and Niihau potentially receiving 6-10 inches (15-25 centimeters) and isolated maximums of 14 inches (36 centimeters). Hawaii's Big Island could see 4-8 inches (10-20 centimeters) of rain, with some areas reaching up to 12 inches (30 centimeters). These rainfall totals could lead to significant flash flooding and mudslides.

Coastal areas on Kauai are also at risk of flooding due to a combination of storm surge and tides, with waters potentially rising up to 3 feet (1 meter) in normally dry areas. Hurricane-force winds extend outward up to 50 miles (85 kilometers) from Lowell's center, while tropical storm-force winds reach up to 175 miles (280 kilometers).

The Kauai Emergency Management Agency has advised residents to take immediate precautions, including filling gas tanks, charging electronic devices, refilling prescriptions, and ensuring adequate supplies of water and food. Residents are also encouraged to be prepared to stay home for several days. In Lihue, Kauai's primary airport town, residents were observed stocking up on essentials, leading to emptying supermarket shelves. A local real estate agent, Lori Benkert, reported boarding up properties and purchasing extra propane for cooking in case of power outages.

Key Takeaways

  • A tropical storm warning has been issued for Kauai and Niihau as Category 3 Hurricane Lowell approaches Hawaii.
  • The islands are bracing for heavy rains, potential flash flooding, mudslides, and coastal storm surge of up to 3 feet.
  • Residents are urged to complete emergency preparations, including stocking supplies and preparing for potential power outages and extended periods at home.

Why It Matters

The approach of Hurricane Lowell poses a significant threat to Hawaii, particularly the islands of Kauai and Niihau. As a major Category 3 storm, Lowell has the potential to cause widespread disruption, property damage, and create dangerous conditions for residents and visitors. The warnings for heavy rainfall, flooding, and mudslides highlight the severe risks to infrastructure and public safety. Preparedness measures are crucial to mitigate the impact and ensure the well-being of the affected communities.
